subject: mathematics_2a
question_text: Find the number of ways of arranging the letters of the word a⁴b³c⁵ in its expanded form.

mark_split.label: Count the letters and the repeats

recall_prompt: Say how you would count the arrangements of the letters of a to the 4, b cubed, c to the 5 written out in full — what you count first and which formula you use.
insider_note: In expanded form a⁴b³c⁵ is a word of 4 + 3 + 5 = 12 letters, so the count is 12!/(4!·3!·5!) — the exponents are letter counts to divide by, not powers to evaluate.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Count the letters and the repeats
steps.margin_note: First mark. Expanded, a⁴b³c⁵ is aaaabbbccccc: 12 letters, a four times, b three times, c five times.
steps.memory_tip: Expanded, a⁴b³c⁵ is aaaabbbccccc — 12 letters. The exponents are counts, not powers to evaluate.
lines: a four times, b three times, c five times.

recall.must_convey: That the expanded word has 4 + 3 + 5 = 12 letters, with a four times, b three times and c five times.
accept: twelve letters, a four times, b three times, c five times
expand it to four a, three b, five c, twelve letters in all
the exponents are the counts, four three and five, total twelve
a nalugu, b moodu, c aidu, total twelve letters
the powers tell how many times each letter repeats

steps.why: Alike letters cannot be told apart, so swapping them does not give a new arrangement. The count of each repeated letter is what the formula divides by, so it must be found before anything else.
common_mistakes: Treating a⁴b³c⁵ as three letters and answering 3! = 6.

steps.label: Apply n!/(p!·q!·r!)

recall.must_convey: That the count is 12 factorial over 4 factorial times 3 factorial times 5 factorial.
accept: twelve factorial over four factorial three factorial five factorial
n factorial by p factorial q factorial r factorial with four three and five
twelve factorial divided by twenty four times six times one twenty
twelve factorial by four factorial into three factorial into five factorial
the answer is twelve factorial over four factorial three factorial five factorial which is twenty seven thousand seven hundred twenty

steps.why: n! counts the arrangements as if every letter were different; each group of p alike letters has been counted p! times over, so dividing by p! for each group leaves the true count.
common_mistakes: Dividing by 4!·3! and forgetting 5! for the c group.
